questions.question: Above what PSI value is a change treated as significant?
Are the PSI thresholds learned from data or documented constants?

documents.text: The drift detector uses Population Stability Index (PSI) on binned distributions for the numeric metrics. Common practice in drift literature treats PSI below 0.1 as no significant change, 0.1 to 0.25 as moderate, and above 0.25 as significant. The thresholds are documented constants, not learned values.

questions.question: What mean shift, in SD units, reaches the alert threshold?
In the Cohen convention, what size of effect is 0.5 SD?

documents.text: Mean shift is measured in pooled standard deviation units. The warning threshold is 0.5 SD and the alert threshold is 1.0 SD. In the Cohen convention, 0.5 SD is a medium effect and 1.0 SD is a large effect. The overall severity for a metric is the higher of the PSI signal and the mean-shift signal.

questions.question: What pass-rate drop counts as a warning signal?
Does a rise in pass rate ever trigger an alert?

documents.text: The pass-rate check compares two proportions with a z statistic. A drop of 0.05 is a warning signal. A drop of 0.10 with a z magnitude above 1.96, the 5 percent two-sided cut-off, is an alert. The check is one-sided: it alerts only on drops, so a rise in pass rate never alerts.

questions.question: What does alpha-large cost per 1,000 output tokens, in dollars?
Are the prices in the table live vendor prices?

documents.text: The price table holds teaching constants stated for the Learn level. They are not live vendor prices and must not be quoted as such. The alpha-small model costs 0.10 dollars per 1,000 input tokens and 0.20 dollars per 1,000 output tokens. The alpha-large model costs 0.50 dollars per 1,000 input tokens and 1.00 dollars per 1,000 output tokens. Cost is computed as prompt tokens over 1000 times the input rate plus completion tokens over 1000 times the output rate, rounded to 6 decimal places.

questions.question: How many characters per token does the proxy assume?
Is the proxy a real tokenizer?

documents.text: The token proxy is a deterministic stand-in, not a real tokenizer. proxy_token_count returns the ceiling of the text length divided by 4, with a minimum of 1 for non-empty text and 0 for empty text. It approximates the common rule of thumb of about 4 characters per token. It must not be quoted as a real tokenizer count for any model.

questions.question: Did the rule raise any false alert in the 50 no-drift control pairs?
In how many of 50 runs did the KS baseline catch the 0.25 SD shift?

documents.text: On simulated request logs at 1,000 records per window, the drift rule raised no false alert in 50 no-drift control pairs. It alerted on both injected drifts. It is weak on small changes: a 0.25 SD latency shift alerted in 15 of 50 runs, where a Kolmogorov-Smirnov baseline caught 50 of 50. Below 500 records per window it false-alarmed in 38 to 50 of 50 controls.

questions.question: How many records per window did decision 0001 set?
What fired medium alerts on the no-drift control at 200 records per window?

documents.text: Decision 0001 raised every drift window to 1,000 records. The first Deep run used 200 records per window, and PSI sampling noise fired medium alerts on the no-drift control. The calibration study later measured the effect: 50 of 50 false alerts at 100 records per window, 38 of 50 at 200, and 0 of 50 from 500 records up. The decision was made after seeing a result, which is one reason the repo is not pre-registered.

questions.expected_answer: next to the code that writes it
questions.question: Where does each result file live under decision 0002?
What does CI prove about every result file?

documents.text: Decision 0002 keeps the code in the level folders: level-1-learn, level-2-build and level-3-deep, with each result file next to the code that writes it. All evidence is generated from fixed seeds, so there is no captured raw data to keep apart. CI proves every result file regenerates unchanged. Moving to a src layout later means updating the tests, the CI reproduce step, the dashboard imports and the release tags together.

questions.question: Within how many days will a vulnerability report get a reply?

questions.expected_answer: Do not open a public issue
questions.question: Should a vulnerability be reported as a public issue?

documents.text: Report a vulnerability privately through the Report a vulnerability button on the repository Security tab. Do not open a public issue for it. You will get a reply within 7 days. The scope is the code in this repository, which uses the Python standard library only and makes no network calls.

questions.question: What was the median CUSUM detection delay, in records?
At a 40 ms latency shift, in how many of 50 runs did the repo rule alert?

documents.text: The calibration study repeats the drift generator over 50 seed pairs per setting. For a latency shift of 20 ms, which is 0.25 SD, the repo rule alerted in 15 of 50 runs while the KS baseline alerted in 50 of 50. For a shift of 40 ms, which is 0.5 SD, both the repo rule and the KS baseline alerted in 50 of 50 runs. A one-sided CUSUM on a latency stream detected a 40 ms shift with a median detection delay of 32 records.

questions.question: What verdict is the repo capped at until a confirmatory cycle runs?
When were the Deep success criteria written relative to the first Deep results?

documents.text: The proposal is not locked. This repo is not pre-registered: the scaffold spec set scope and acceptance criteria but no hypotheses or pass lines, and the Deep success criteria were written in the same commit as the first Deep results. Under the portfolio standard the repo is capped at Functional until a confirmatory cycle runs under a newly locked proposal.

questions.question: What happens to corrupt lines when the store loads?
Which two latency percentiles does the dashboard show?

documents.text: The LogStore is a persistent JSONL store for records and spans. One file holds every line as a JSON object tagged with a type field of record or span. Corrupt lines are skipped on load and counted. The dashboard is generated from stored records and shows totals, a per-model table, and p50 and p95 latency.

note: Every document is a faithful excerpt or tight paraphrase of the named source file in this repository. Every expected_answer is a verbatim substring of its document (checked case-insensitively by tests/test_live_observability.py), so the answer check measures whether the model found the answer in the document it was given.
